tasks.short: Check clocked hours, overtime and allowances against rosters and the CAO before they go into AFAS.

today.trigger: Weekly and four-weekly period close; site supervisors send corrected hours lists.
steps: Export clock data per site (Rotterdam, Tilburg, Venlo) into Excel
Compare against shift rosters and approved overtime mails in Outlook
Apply CAO rules for shift, night and weekend allowances by hand
Chase supervisors in Teams about missing or odd entries
Key approved mutations into AFAS Profit
drudgery: Matching rows between three site exports and rosters
Re-checking allowance rules that never change
Chasing the same supervisors every period
today.time_sinks: Matching hours to rosters line by line and waiting for supervisor answers on missing punches.

lenses.faster: A rules script matches clock data to rosters and computes CAO allowances; only mismatches reach the specialist.
lenses.autonomous: At each period close the check runs on its own, posts clean hours to an AFAS import file and sends each supervisor a list of their open exceptions.
lenses.ambitious: Check hours daily instead of per period, so a missed punch is fixed the next morning rather than as a correction after payday.
lenses.joy: No more row matching; what is left is sorting out the odd cases with supervisors.
lenses.options: Show the specialist two or three plausible readings of a broken punch (forgot to clock out, double shift, swap) with the pay effect of each.
lenses.altitude: The specialist maintains the allowance rule table per CAO and site and reviews the exception rate per site.
reach: Give site supervisors a self-service view of their team's open exceptions (operations)
Feed approved overtime into labour-cost reporting for the FP&A Analyst

tasks.human_edge: Judging a disputed punch with a supervisor and knowing when a CAO clause applies to an unusual shift.
tasks.pattern_why: Hours, rosters and CAO allowance rules are structured and can be written down; output is checkable per line.

in_practice.trigger: Daily after clock data lands, and a final run at period close.
steps: Load clock exports and rosters per site
Match punches to shifts and compute allowances from the CAO rule table
Write clean lines to an AFAS Profit mutation import
Send exceptions to supervisors and the specialist
Specialist resolves exceptions and releases the import
in_practice.human_gate: Payroll Specialist releases the import file and decides every exception.
data_needed: CAO allowance rules per site and contract
in_practice.logs_to: Exception log per period on SharePoint with who decided what.

evidence.claim: Payroll calculation stays deterministic and rules-based; AI is used around it.
AFAS Profit can take payroll mutations through an import or connector instead of manual keying.

risks: Rule table drifts from a new CAO and pays allowances wrong for months
Works council consent is needed for processing time data (WOR art. 27)
Bad clock data gives false confidence if exceptions are tuned too loosely
research_questions: What share of period lines today are changed after the first check?
Can the clock systems at all three sites export the same fields daily?
Are the allowance rules of both CAOs complete enough to write as a table without interpretation?

tasks.short: Enter variable pay items and deductions into AFAS and check the gross-to-net outcome.

today.trigger: Each four-weekly or monthly payroll run.
steps: Collect variable items: overtime, allowances, bonuses, garnishments, expense claims
Enter them as mutations in AFAS Profit
Run the trial calculation
Spot-check gross-to-net on a sample in Excel
Correct and rerun
drudgery: Keying items that already exist in another file
Manual spot checks of the same cases each run
today.time_sinks: Re-keying and rerunning the trial calculation after small corrections.

lenses.faster: Variable items arrive as an import, AFAS calculates, and a scripted comparison against last run replaces manual spot checks.
lenses.autonomous: The trial run starts when all inputs are in, and a comparison report waits for the specialist.
lenses.ambitious: Run a full trial calculation weekly so errors are found before close, not in the last two days.
lenses.joy: Typing and rerunning go away; the specialist works on the cases where the numbers move.
lenses.options: For a disputed item, show the net effect of the two or three possible treatments side by side.
lenses.altitude: The specialist owns the wage component setup in AFAS and the comparison rules, not the entry.
reach: Prepare the payroll journal check for the Accountant
Answer the Compensation and Benefits Specialist's cost questions from run data

tasks.human_edge: Accountability for correct pay, and judgement on unusual items such as garnishments and back pay.
tasks.pattern_why: Gross-to-net is a rules engine in AFAS; generated calculations are not acceptable, so automation is import plus checks.

in_practice.trigger: All input sources marked complete for the period.
steps: Import variable items into AFAS Profit
Run trial calculation
Compare each employee's gross and net with the previous run and flag moves outside set bands
Specialist reviews flags and approves the run
in_practice.human_gate: Payroll Specialist approves the run before payment files go to Rabobank.
in_practice.logs_to: Run approval record and flag list on SharePoint.

evidence.claim: Calculation stays deterministic; AI is limited to checks around it.
'A good guess isn't good enough' in payroll; Workday keeps calculation rules-based.

risks: Over-trust in the import hides a wrongly set wage component
January tax table and CAO changes break comparison bands
research_questions: How many minutes per run go to keying versus checking?
Does Noordhaven's AFAS licence include the import connector for payroll mutations?
How many reruns per period happen today and why?

tasks.short: Keep leave balances right: holiday, ATV, special leave and sick days, per CAO and contract.

today.trigger: Leave requests, sick and recovery reports, contract changes, year end.
steps: Check leave requests and approvals in AFAS
Correct balances for part-time changes and CAO extra days
Record sick and recovery dates passed on by HR
Answer balance questions by mail
Settle expiring and remaining leave at year end
drudgery: Answering 'how many days do I have' mails
today.time_sinks: Year-end expiry and pro-rata recalculation for part-timers and flex-to-permanent moves.

lenses.faster: Entitlement rules per CAO and contract are set up once in AFAS; pro-rata and expiry run automatically.
lenses.autonomous: Balances recalculate on any contract change, and employees get a reminder before statutory leave expires.
lenses.ambitious: Every employee sees a correct balance at any time, ending most leave questions.
lenses.joy: No more recalculating by hand; what is left is the odd case.
lenses.options: Show managers what a leave request does to team coverage and to the person's year balance.
lenses.altitude: The specialist designs and tests the entitlement rules and audits a sample each quarter.
reach: Give the HR Administrator a checked balance view for employee questions
Feed absence data to the verzuim process run by HR Business Partners

tasks.human_edge: Applying CAO clauses to unusual cases and handling sick-leave data carefully.
tasks.pattern_why: Leave entitlements follow CAO and statutory rules on structured contract data.

in_practice.trigger: Contract change, leave approval, sick or recovery report, year end.
steps: Apply entitlement rules to contract hours and seniority
Recalculate balances and expiry
Flag negative or unusual balances
Specialist checks flags
in_practice.human_gate: Payroll Specialist decides flagged balances and year-end payouts.
data_needed: Leave and absence records (no medical details)
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS mutation history and a quarterly sample audit sheet.

evidence.claim: Two CAOs and seasonal flex staff multiply rule variants; rules should stay explicit.

risks: Medical details in absence records breach AVG; record dates only
Wrong rule for one CAO group affects hundreds of balances at once
research_questions: Are the leave rules of both CAOs fully configured in AFAS today, or partly kept in Excel?
How many leave balance questions does HR get per month?
How many balance corrections happen at year end?

tasks.short: Process tax credit choices, transfers and resignations into AFAS payroll records.

today.trigger: Forms and mails from employees, managers and HR: loonheffingskorting form, transfer, resignation letter.
steps: Read the form or mail
Check it against the contract and HR record
Enter the change in AFAS with the right start or end date
Calculate final pay items for leavers (leave payout, holiday allowance)
File the document
drudgery: Retyping data from PDFs and mails
Looking up the same contract fields each time
today.time_sinks: Unclear or late resignation and transfer messages that need follow-up.

lenses.faster: A model reads the incoming form or mail and proposes the AFAS mutation with dates filled in; the specialist checks and confirms.
lenses.autonomous: Incoming documents in the payroll mailbox are read on arrival, and missing fields go back to the sender automatically.
lenses.ambitious: Every leaver's final pay is calculated and checked before the last day, not after.
lenses.joy: No retyping; the specialist checks proposals and handles the unclear ones.
lenses.options: For a leaver, show the final pay under different end dates or leave settlement choices.
lenses.altitude: The specialist maintains the field mapping and checks the share of proposals accepted unchanged.
reach: Take over contract-change mutations from the HR Administrator
Prepare final settlement figures for the HR Business Partner in exit cases

tasks.human_edge: Spotting when a 'resignation' is really a dispute, and judging dates and settlements.
tasks.pattern_why: Input is unstructured mail and PDFs; output is a structured, checkable mutation in a fixed workflow.

in_practice.trigger: New document in the payroll mailbox or an HR workflow in AFAS.
steps: Model extracts employee, change type, dates and fields
Script checks against the AFAS record
Proposal appears in a review queue
Specialist approves and the mutation is posted
in_practice.logs_to: Review queue with original document, proposal and approver.

evidence.claim: Timesheet and leave documents suit llm_step intake inside a rules workflow.
AFAS shows wage-component history, which supports checking proposals.

risks: Model reads a wrong date and a leaver is paid an extra month
Personal data sent to an external model needs a processor agreement and works council consent (WOR 27)
research_questions: How many such documents arrive per month, and in what formats?
What share arrive incomplete today?
Can extraction run inside Noordhaven's Microsoft 365 tenant?

tasks.short: Pre-run check: find and fix odd pay amounts before the payroll is approved.

today.trigger: Trial run before each payroll close.
steps: Export trial results to Excel
Compare with last period by eye and with pivot tables
Look into big swings, missing pension, negative nets
Correct in AFAS and rerun
Note fixes for the controller
drudgery: Building the same pivot tables each period
Scanning hundreds of lines for swings
today.time_sinks: Explaining each swing by digging through mutations.

lenses.faster: Fixed rules flag swings, missing pension, double leaver pay and pay under minimum wage; a model writes a short explanation per flag from the mutation history.
lenses.autonomous: Checks run on every trial calculation and send a ranked list of exceptions with explanations.
lenses.ambitious: Track first-time-right pay runs and corrections per run as team metrics, and make them visible each month.
lenses.joy: The specialist stops scanning and starts investigating real anomalies.
lenses.options: For each flag, show likely causes ranked by evidence in the mutation history.
lenses.altitude: The specialist designs the check set, tunes thresholds and adds a rule after every correction found late.
reach: Hand the Controller a documented pre-run control for the audit file
Give People Analytics a correction trend per site

tasks.human_edge: Deciding whether a flagged amount is wrong, and owning the sign-off.
tasks.pattern_why: Detection is deterministic; explaining each exception from mutation history is unstructured text to a checkable note.

steps: Run rule checks on trial results
Model drafts an explanation per exception from mutations and contract changes
Specialist reviews, corrects and approves
Approved run and exception notes are stored
in_practice.human_gate: Payroll Specialist approves every exception before the run is final.
in_practice.logs_to: Per-run exception register on SharePoint, shared with the Controller.

evidence.claim: Production checks for gross pay swings, stopped pension, double leaver pay and below minimum wage.
Workday Payroll Agent will flag items outside defined parameters for payroll to check.

risks: Plausible but wrong explanations lead the specialist to accept an error
Too many flags and people stop reading them
research_questions: How many corrections per run were found after payment in the last 12 months?
Which of the four PayCaptain checks would have caught them?
Do explanations save time compared with opening the mutation history directly?

tasks.short: Fill in or correct arrival and departure times, including paper and agency timesheets for flex workers.

today.trigger: Missing punches, paper timesheets from sites, flex hours in agency portals.
steps: Collect paper or photo timesheets from site offices
Download flex hours from three agency portals
Type times into Excel or AFAS
Check missing punches with supervisors
drudgery: Logging into three portals with different formats
today.time_sinks: Peak season, when 300 flex workers' hours come in on different sheets.

lenses.faster: A model reads photos and portal exports into one table; a script checks it against rosters.
lenses.autonomous: Uploads from site offices and portal exports are processed on arrival; only unreadable or conflicting lines reach the specialist.
lenses.ambitious: Get rid of paper sheets by moving every site to a clock, so this task mostly disappears.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses typing handwriting; what is left is fixing a few conflicts.
lenses.options: Compare cost and effort of reading paper versus putting clocks in the remaining places.
lenses.altitude: The specialist sets the data standard for hours and asks agencies to deliver in it.
reach: Check agency hours before the Bookkeeper pays agency invoices
Give site managers hours data for planning

tasks.human_edge: Settling conflicts between what the worker, supervisor and agency say.
tasks.pattern_why: Handwritten sheets and differing portal formats are unstructured; the output is a structured hours table checked by rules.

in_practice.trigger: Upload of a timesheet photo or new hours in an agency portal.
steps: Model extracts name, date, start and end times
Script matches against roster and agency order
Conflicts go to the specialist
Approved hours are imported
in_practice.human_gate: Payroll Specialist approves hours with conflicts; supervisors confirm disputed times.
in_practice.logs_to: Hours register with source image and approver.

evidence.claim: In AFAS Flex, payroll lines approve automatically once a person approves the declaration, a rule after a human gate.
Reading handwritten timesheets is feasible with current vision models.

risks: Using time data to score people can be high-risk under the AI Act from 2 December 2027
Monitoring with time data needs works council consent (WOR 27)
research_questions: How many paper timesheets come in per week in peak season?
Can the three agencies export hours in one format?
What is the cost of clocks at the sites still on paper?

tasks.short: Set up new hires in AFAS payroll from the offer, contract, ID, bank and tax forms.

today.trigger: Accepted offer in Recruitee and signed contract from HR.
steps: Get offer and contract details from Recruitee and SharePoint
Collect ID copy, bank account and loonheffingskorting form
Enter employee, contract, pay scale and pension in AFAS
Check against CAO scale
Confirm to HR that payroll is ready
drudgery: Retyping offer data already in Recruitee
today.time_sinks: Missing forms before the first pay run, especially in seasonal hiring peaks.

lenses.faster: An agent pulls the accepted offer from Recruitee, reads the uploaded documents and prepares the AFAS employee record.
lenses.autonomous: On offer acceptance the agent requests missing documents from the new hire and reminds them until complete.
lenses.ambitious: Every new hire is paid correctly in their first pay run, supporting the 90-day retention goal.
lenses.joy: No retyping or chasing; the specialist checks a complete file.
lenses.options: Show the scale and step options under the CAO for an offer before it is made.
lenses.altitude: The specialist owns the onboarding data checklist and the mapping from Recruitee to AFAS.
reach: Take over employee record setup from the HR Administrator
Check offers against CAO scales for Recruiters before sending

tasks.human_edge: Checking ID documents and judging scale placement where the CAO leaves room.
tasks.pattern_why: Several systems, documents and follow-ups with the new hire; a person approves the record before it counts.

steps: Pull offer data from Recruitee
Request and read ID, bank and tax forms
Check scale against CAO table
Draft AFAS employee and contract record
Specialist approves; record goes live
in_practice.human_gate: Payroll Specialist checks ID and approves the record before the first run.
in_practice.logs_to: Onboarding checklist per hire in AFAS or SharePoint.

evidence.claim: Agent-style onboarding across ATS and HR core is plausible with current APIs.

risks: ID copies handled outside AFAS breach AVG retention rules
A wrong scale step underpays a new hire from day one
Works council consent for a bot reading personnel data (WOR 27(1)(k))
research_questions: How many new hires were not correctly paid in their first run last year?
Does Recruitee's API expose offer details needed for AFAS?
How long does it take today from acceptance to a complete payroll record?

tasks.short: Pull together hours, production and pay data into period overviews for payroll and finance.

today.trigger: Period close and requests from finance and site managers.
steps: Export hours, flex hours and run results
Combine in Excel per site and cost centre
Reconcile totals with AFAS and agency invoices
Send overviews to Controller and site managers
drudgery: Rebuilding the same Excel workbook each period
today.time_sinks: Reconciling agency hours with invoices and with AFAS.

lenses.faster: A fixed pipeline combines sources and reconciles totals; Power BI shows the result.
lenses.autonomous: The pipeline runs nightly with the AFAS extract and flags differences above a threshold.
lenses.ambitious: Labour cost per site and per pallet handled, available weekly instead of per period.
lenses.joy: No more workbook rebuilding; the specialist looks only at differences.
lenses.options: Show labour cost scenarios for the season with different flex and overtime mixes.
lenses.altitude: The specialist owns data definitions and reconciliation rules, not the workbook.
reach: Match agency invoices to approved hours for the Bookkeeper
Supply labour-cost inputs to FP&A Analysts
Prepare pay data for the yearly gender pay gap report

tasks.human_edge: Explaining differences to finance and deciding which source is right.
tasks.pattern_why: Structured sources with fixed joins and reconciliation rules; output is checkable totals.

steps: Load hours, flex hours and run data
Join on employee and cost centre
Reconcile totals and agency invoices
Publish to Power BI and flag differences
in_practice.human_gate: Payroll Specialist signs off period totals sent to the Controller.
in_practice.logs_to: Reconciliation report per period in Power BI and SharePoint.

evidence.claim: Gross-to-net, filings and reconciliations belong in deterministic software at autonomy 4–5.
Noordhaven reports its gender pay gap yearly, first over 2027 pay, due 7 June 2028.

risks: Agency portal formats change and break the pipeline silently
Production data per person can drift into performance scoring (AI Act, works council)
research_questions: How many hours per period go into the overview workbook today?
Can agency portals deliver hours and invoices by API or scheduled export?
What differences between agency invoices and approved hours were found last year?

role.altitude: From entering and checking pay data to owning the payroll rule set, the pre-run controls and the data standards that AFAS, the agencies and the sites must meet; the specialist signs off runs on exceptions, not line by line.
reach: Match agency invoices to approved flex hours (Bookkeeper)
Payroll journal and wage tax reconciliation (Accountant)
Employee records for new hires and changes (HR Administrator)
Pay data and checks for the gender pay gap report and pay information requests (Compensation and Benefits Specialist, People Analytics)
Labour-cost inputs and season scenarios (FP&A Analyst)
Explained answers to payslip questions, with AI disclosure (HR Administrator)
role.ceiling_note: About half of the eight tasks' roughly 780 hours a year can go; the pay-run sign-off, CAO interpretation, disputed hours and legal liability stay with the person. Limits are works council consent for tools reading time and personnel data, AVG rules on ID and absence data, yearly rule changes (CAO, January tax tables), and staff reluctance about AI in pay.
skills_to_grow: Writing pay and CAO rules as testable tables
AFAS Profit configuration, imports and connectors
Power Query or SQL for reconciliations
Pay transparency law (EU 2023/970) and gender pay gap reporting
AVG, works council and AI Act requirements for payroll tooling
role.ambitious_version: First-time-right pay for every employee and flex worker each period, corrections per run tracked to near zero, every payslip line explainable on request, agency hours matched to invoices before payment, and the 2027 gender pay gap report and pay information requests produced from checked data, not built by hand.
